stemMarkdown: A man travels from A to B at 40 km/h and returns along the same road at 50 km/h. What is his average speed (in km/h) for the whole journey? (Round to 4 decimal places.)
solutionMarkdown: Average speed is total distance over total time, not the average of the two speeds. Taking the one-way distance as $d$: time $= \dfrac{d}{40} + \dfrac{d}{50}$, so average speed $= \dfrac{2d}{d/40 + d/50} = \dfrac{2 \times 40 \times 50}{40 + 50} = 44.4444$.
altSolutionMarkdown: For equal distances the answer is the harmonic mean. The plain average $\dfrac{40 + 50}{2} = 45.0$ is the classic wrong answer, and it is always too high.
